subject: Re: Great House Farm
source: Original email in the family's Gmail (read-only export); contact details redacted.
text:
Mr Egan,

Thank you for your response and for confirming that the Council's minute
books from 1982 onwards were deposited with Glamorgan Archives in 2002.

I note your reliance upon Section 21 FOIA in respect of records already
accessible through Glamorgan Archives. I shall pursue those records
directly with the archive.

However, my request was not limited to council minutes. I also requested
disclosure of any correspondence, clerk's notes, memoranda, photographs,
maps, plans, committee papers, archived files or other records held by the
Council concerning:

Ty Mawr (Great House Farm), Llandough;
the associated farm lands;
the Williams family;
Billy Buckler, [member of the public] and members of the Buckler family;
BP Properties Ltd v Buckler and related matters.

Accordingly, I would be grateful if you could clarify:

Whether the Council presently holds any records responsive to the above
request other than the deposited minute books;
If such records exist, whether they remain in the Council's possession or
were transferred to another archive or repository;
If no such records are held, whether this is because they were never
created, were transferred elsewhere, or were subsequently destroyed;
Whether the Council retains any record of Billy Buckler addressing the
Council, whether in minutes, correspondence, agenda papers, clerk's notes
or any other form.

For the avoidance of doubt, I am content to receive a simple confirmation
of whether such records are held and their location, rather than requiring
the Council to undertake extensive historical research.

Thank you for your assistance and I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours sincerely,

Requester 



On Sun, 14 Jun 2026, 13:04 Paul Egan, <[email redacted]> wrote:

> Dear Requester,
>
> I have undertaken a reasonable search of our records and would advise you
> as follows:
>
> a) The minutes of all council minutes for the period in question were
> deposited in the Glamorgan Records Office in 2002. These cover the period
> from 1982 when Llandough Community Council was first formed. Prior to that
> time, the community of Llandough was included in the remit of Penarth Town
> Council. The relevant web-link which shows the information held is :
> perihttps://glamarchives.gov.uk/od
>
> b) You are able to visit the Glamorgan Records Office in Cardiff by
> appointment and the web-link to find details of their location is:
> https://glamarchives.gov.uk/
>
> Section 21 of the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) is an absolute
> exemption that allows public authorities to refuse a request if the
> requested information is already reasonably accessible to the applicant by
> other means. This avoids duplicating effort and prevents authorities from
> acting as personal research services.
>
> c) I would suggest that you access the Llandough Community Council's
> website for historical information about the community of Llandough -
> web-link is :
>
> https://www.llandough-cc.co.uk/Buildings_of_Significance_in_our_Community_25590.aspx
>
> Kind regards,
>

> concerning the property and family were discussed by Llandough Community

>
> I am attempting to reconstruct the historical chain of occupation,
> ownership, administration and public record concerning the property, family

>
> https://bpvsbuckler.datro.xyz
>
> Accordingly, I request disclosure of all records held by Llandough
> Community Council, regardless of date, concerning:
>
>    - Ty Mawr (Great House), Llandough;
>    - the associated farm lands and any connected parcels;
>    - the Williams family and successors in occupation;
>    - Billy Buckler, [member of the public] and members of the Buckler family;
>    - historical ownership, occupation, tenancy, possession, planning,
>    access, acquisition, disposal, development, disputes or representations;
>    - BP v Buckler and related matters;
>    - any meetings in which Billy Buckler addressed the Council.
>
> This request includes, but is not limited to:
>
>    - minute books;
>    - agendas;
>    - correspondence;
>    - maps;
>    - plans;
>    - asset registers;
>    - committee papers;
>    - land schedules;
>    - photographs;
>    - memoranda;
>    - clerk notes;
>    - archived files;
>    - transferred records;
>    - records held by third-party archives on the Council's behalf.
>

>
>    1. Whether older records were transferred elsewhere;
>    2. The archive location;
>    3. Whether records were destroyed and under what retention policy;
>    4. The earliest records held concerning the property.
>
> My understanding is that family occupation and acquisition history extends
> substantially earlier, potentially to the seventeenth century, and I am
> seeking to establish the documentary chain.
>
> I am confident that our claim to the fee simple absolute manorial title
> still stands and no amount of time, fraud, purgergy, court "mistakes", gaps
> in records, demolition of our home, erasure of history (like Marconi
> staying with us while inventing radio), acts of terrorism, human rights
> violations, lawfare, nor proceedural unfairness and supression or
> witholding of information and possible murder of members of my family has
> changed that fact. It appears our title was stolen and this is a position
> grandmother held until 1982 when she conveniently died in the 2 week window
> she had to challenge BP's registrstion of our land in their name with the
> land registry.
>
> ITV also recently declassified and published coverage too:
>
> https://youtu.be/4GXmR7mAas0?feature=shared
>
> This is a terrorist/ hostage situation so far as I see. My dispossessed
> family are your hostages not constituents. They are too frightened to even
> speak up about this matter. I require of your department some effort to
> revisit your postion.
>
> My research tells me that the councillor at the time said, prior to my
> father's death, that the situation with BP would result in a death. I
> believe that was concerning the conflict with Bailiffs, Police and possibly
> SAS.
>
> I have submitted a FOI to the MOD too. The Ministry of Justice are also on
> notice and imply this matter is being investigated.
>
> If not me, who? If not now, when?

> Sir/Ma'am,
>
> I am your constituent, living [location redacted]. I am writing to request your
> assistance in reviewing a historic legal matter involving my family: *BP
> Properties Ltd v Buckler (1987)*, relating to Great House Farm, Llandough.
>
> My family lived on, cared for and claimed to own that farm for
> generations. The events surrounding the 1987 case resulted in the loss of
> our home and land, and left several members of my family deeply affected.
> Recent research I have undertaken has revealed significant procedural
> inconsistencies, historical irregularities, unanswered questions regarding
> corporate identity, unverified service of key documents, and heritage
> considerations relating to the site.
>
> I have attached a short report summarising SOME of these issues. I am
> requesting your help in identifying the appropriate bodies—legal,
> historical, or governmental—who may be able to independently review the
> historical record to ensure fairness, accuracy, and transparency.
>
> My interest is not solely personal; Great House Farm has a heritage
> significance to Wales, including documented accounts that Guglielmo Marconi
> stayed there while experimenting with early radio technology. I believe
> this should form part of our preserved historical record.
>
> By way of background, I am a veteran and have served both in the Armed
> Forces and recently with the Vale of Glamorgan Council. My intention is
> simply to seek clarity, proper review, and justice where appropriate. I
> would be grateful for your guidance on the correct avenues to pursue.
>
> Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to your response.
>
> Yours sincerely,
>
